overview: This bill would require federal regulators to study partnerships between banks and financial technology (fintech) companies, which provide services such as payment apps and online lending. The Federal Reserve, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) would examine how these partnerships affect competition, innovation, consumer protection and the creation of new banks, and what changes to laws or rules could help such partnerships work well. The National Credit Union Administration would do a similar study of credit union and fintech partnerships. Each study would be due to Congress within one year. As of February 25, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was awaiting a vote by the full House.
for: Supporters say a clear look at bank-fintech partnerships could help smaller banks and credit unions compete and give customers more products, while pointing out where rules stand in the way.
against: Critics say the study is framed around promoting these partnerships, which could tilt it away from the consumer-protection problems that some bank-fintech arrangements have raised.
